brief_summary: Two-column do/don't map under the H2 'What the dye can plausibly change — and what it can't'. Left column (amber checks): optical tint/translucency, and color that survives wear because it isn't a surface coat. Right column (caution-red crosses): claimed 'denser plastic', claimed 'better damping', and claimed 'smoother glide' — each annotated with the actual mechanism (tolerancing, resin pairing, factory lube). A dashed amber note box states that colorant load is too small a fraction of resin weight to move bulk density or damping.
data_sources: gateron-ink-housings-deep-dive.mdx § 'What the dye can plausibly change — and what it can't' — 'Colorant loading in injection-molded parts is typically a small fraction of the resin's weight ... Don't credit it for denser plastic, better damping, or a warmer sound ... Any acoustic or tactile difference ... is far more likely to be the tolerancing, the lube, or the resin pairing doing the work.'
